cards.text: Peter comes to Jesus with a question. How many times should he forgive a brother who sins against him? Then he answers it himself: “Up to seven times?” I bet he thought that was VERY generous.

cards.question: Peter offers to forgive his brother up to seven times. Jesus tells Peter that seven times is enough.

cards.text: Jesus says, “I tell you, not just seven times, but seventy-seven times!” Peter thought he was running a marathon, and Jesus just told him that was the WARM-UP.
Then Jesus tells a story: the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants. Audit day, friend, and the first debtor is walking in.

cards.question: The first servant brought before the king owes a huge debt. How much does he owe?
The servant can't pay a debt like that. What does the master order?

answers.text: Sell him and his family and everything
Make him work off the whole debt
Send him away from the kingdom

cards.question: Facing the loss of his family and everything he owns, what does the servant do?

answers.text: Falls on his knees and begs

cards.text: “Have patience with me,” he begs, “and I will pay back everything.” Ten thousand talents, friend, and that's like me promising to pay off the whole bakery with the crumbs in my apron pocket.

cards.question: The servant begs his master for patience. The master gives him more time to pay it all back.

cards.text: His master had compassion on him, forgave his debt and released him. The WHOLE thing, gone, and on his way out he finds a fellow servant who owes him a hundred denarii.

cards.question: Fresh off being forgiven, the servant cancels the hundred denarii his fellow servant owes him.

cards.text: Instead, he grabs the man and starts choking him: “Pay back what you owe me!” The ink on his OWN forgiveness isn't even dry.
His fellow servant falls down and begs him, “Have patience with me, and I will pay you back.” Friend… where have I heard that one before?

cards.question: The forgiven servant refuses to wait and has his fellow servant thrown into ___ until he can pay his debt.
The other servants see what happened. They are greatly ___, and they go and tell their ___ all of it.

cards.text: The master summons him: “You wicked servant! I forgave all your debt because you begged me.” Ohhh, friend. He just got called into the boss's office, and the boss already KNOWS.

cards.question: What does the master say this servant should have done for his fellow servant?

answers.text: Shown him mercy the way he was shown mercy
Brought the matter to the master first
Let the other servants settle the debt

cards.text: In anger, the master hands him over to the jailers to be tortured until he repays all he owed. The whole debt he was forgiven is back on him.

cards.question: Jesus ends the story with its point: “That is how My heavenly Father will treat each of you unless you forgive your brother from your ___.”
